name: chart
behavior: None — the plot itself is a graphic. Accessibility comes from a text alternative, not from the drawing: the root is role=img with an accessible name and description, and the same data is exposed as a visually-hidden table so keyboard and screen-reader users get the values. Interactive tooltips follow the APG tooltip pattern (shown on hover AND on focus, dismissible with Esc, never trapping the pointer); legend entries that toggle series are toggle buttons with aria-pressed. Series are distinguished by more than hue — pattern, marker shape or direct labels — so the chart survives colour-vision differences and monochrome print.

one line/bar/area/slice set; the Nth series takes the Nth data slot in order — the ordinal set is the only place numbered tokens are legal (contract/naming.md)

parts.note: takes the same data slot as its series
one series' value at the hovered position; type-data keeps digits aligned across rows
the visually-hidden table carrying the same values — required, not optional: it is what makes the graphic accessible

anatomyNotes: Intersection of shadcn Chart (Recharts wrapper: ChartContainer/ChartTooltipContent/ChartLegendContent, series colours injected as --color-<key> from chart-1..5) and Salt's highcharts-theme (Highcharts option overrides supplying a categorical palette, axis/grid/tooltip styling). The two share no code and no component API — only the parts above — which is exactly why the anatomy is worth writing: it is the contract that lets a Recharts theme and a Highcharts theme render the same chart. The registry widens shadcn's 5-colour palette to the contract's data-1..12 ordinal set (themes rotate beyond 12). Chart TYPE (line/bar/area/pie/scatter) is not a variant axis: it changes which parts are present, not how they are themed; a pie chart simply has no axis parts. The plotting library is an implementation choice, never anatomy.
